_doc_walkSceneKey: the town's EXPLORABLE scene key — stated role, not inferred (district fixed-camera bundles carry the whole town's collision, so pad names cannot identify the walk scene). This is the real-time DEVELOPER view; the game routes players into playSceneKey. Built by tools/emb_blockout.py, exported by tools/emb_export.py.
_doc_playSceneKey: the scene the GAME sends players to — the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF grammar this project exists for). Deliberately separate from walkSceneKey: the real-time bundle stays the developer's explore view, and which of the two the scene graph wires is a data choice, not a naming coincidence.
_doc_cameraFile: the hand-authored camera INTENT for playSceneKey. tools/cine_solve.mjs --town emberbrook solves it against this map + the emb-walk walk geometry into emberbrook.cameras.solved.json — the one numeric truth cine_bake.py and play3d.html both read.
premise: The home village: a valley farming settlement gathered around its living Heartlight — one of the last — where the village brook meets the river. Warm, low, earthbound; everything Dellhollow is not. The river is the story's spine: Vesper arrives along it, and leaves through the Sigil Gate to follow it downstream.
units: world units (1u ~ 1m). Axes: x = west-east, y = south-north, z = height (village sits on a gentle rise, z 0..3).

mapDiscovery.rule: Entering a parcel's scene reveals it and its mapVisible landmarks (Vesper inks the map as she walks).

landmarks.name: The Old Gate
landmarks.note: SHIPPED CANON (chapter1.js + STORY.md §1): 'the Old Gate' is what every line calls it; the SIGILS are the twin plates in the ground before it (built as separate props) that open only for two standing them together. Sealed at story start; opens in Ch1; downstream road+river beyond. | TERRAIN RULING 2026-08-01 (user): the Old Gate is the BOTTLENECK between the valley and two mountain cliff bluffs — its masonry built wall-to-wall into living rock so there is no way around; the river/brook exit the valley through the same pinch (a barred water-arch or alongside), and the shadowed gorge beyond IS the road toward Dellhollow. The north end of the valley funnels: forested bluffs converge, the wood climbs their slopes. Concept art variants in docs/qa/emberbrook/concepts/ (notch / valleys-end / ancient-seal), user choosing; blockout carries coarse bluff massing now, dressed cliffs follow the chosen concept. | DESIGN REFINEMENT 2026-08-01 (user): NOT a drain beside the gate — the river runs DIRECTLY PARALLEL to the road and flows UNDER the Old Gate itself: one wide structure spanning the whole notch, twin doors over the road, heavy DRAINAGE BARS (barred water-arches) over the river's passage beside them. Water passes through the gate; people must pass through the doors. GEOGRAPHY STATUS: the water-gap/hanging-valley reading is PROPOSED, not user-ratified — an overworld draft is being built so the user can judge it against their own vision of how the land leads to Dellhollow. Do not hard-bake overworld-dependent facts beyond this valley. | REFINEMENT 2 (user): the water passage is NOT an arch — arches are for humans. The drainage grate sits LOW, at water level only (a culvert grate slightly taller than the waterline), with plain coursed masonry wall above it. Only the road's doorway is arched. | SECLUSION RULING 2026-08-01 (user): the gate is TOO CLOSE to the town center. It moves to a genuinely secluded position — a quiet, wooded, incident-free stretch between the town's last warmth (the barn/dovecote area) and the court, designed as a MEASURED environment shift: village roofs fall out of sight past a threshold, lamp warmth ends at the barn, the forest closes in, then the sealed gate. Builder proposes the new gate/court/trailhead coordinates (notch, bluffs, and river tail move together) for the coordinator's stamp.

impliedScale._doc: USER RULING 2026-07-31: Emberbrook must READ as a lovely, lively town with deep history and a vibrant community — that is what a Heartlight DOES for a town — while chapter one stays focused and tight. Build the town to HINT at being much larger than the playable area: the player does not (and should not) have access to the whole town. Techniques, in canon order of preference: (1) non-walkable massing beyond every playable edge — further rooftops, chimney smoke, lit windows, hillside cottages, always composed into the camera frames; (2) lanes that visibly CONTINUE but are closed at the threshold (festival carts, stacked barrels, a hedge stile — soft, believable closures, never invisible walls); (3) at the Kindling Hour the square is CROWDED with background villagers — non-interactable or barely so; named cast are the interactive minority. The walk network stays exactly as tight as the parcels; the LOOK says big, the WALK says chapter one. | DENSIFICATION RULING 2026-08-01 (user, at 2x review): the village interior itself is TOO SPARSE — the large/populated/lively directive applies INSIDE the bounds, not only at the rim. Blockout-level implementation: deterministic INFILL of non-enterable background homes and structures filling the space between the playable lanes (clusters of 2-4 cottages with gardens, hedgerows, outbuildings, field strips) so every frame reads as a town, not houses on a lawn; closed lanes lead INTO visible clusters (a lane that ends at three more roofs says 'more town'); density gradient — thickest around Festival Square and Home Row, thinning toward the Gate Field and the wood. All infill is lm_-class massing at blockout, real dressed buildings at the district pass; never walkable, never enterable, GateGrid-gated off every lane and area. Target: from any playable lane, 2+ non-playable roofs visible in most directions. | REFINEMENT 2026-08-01 (user, from the mid-build snapshot): the infill overcorrected into unrealistic clutter — cottages packed wall-to-wall. A village cottage is a HOUSEHOLD: each infill home gets its own garden plot (hedge or fence), a fruit tree or two, a shed/woodpile, and a visible access path/track (non-walkable geometry is fine, but nobody builds a house with no way to reach it — tracks may join the real lanes or fade into implied ones). Spacing reads village-true: roughly 6-12 m between cottages, varied, with the FOREST filling between garden plots rather than more houses. Density comes from LIFE per household, not roofs per square metre. The 2+-roofs-visible target stands, met by depth and arrangement, not packing.

laneIncident._doc: USER RULING 2026-08-01: with distances doubled, lanes need MID-LANE INCIDENT to pace the walk — 'a cart, a shrine, a neighbor's fence' class of thing. Implementation is the district pass's dressing layer (post-blockout-ratification): every lane longer than ~15 m gets 1-2 incidents of domestic, familiar life — a handcart, a woodpile, a fence gate, a bench, laundry, beehives, a stile, apple crates — placed by SEARCH off the lane edge (never on walk surface), gated like all solids. LORE BUDGET NOTE: no invented shrine-institutions — in this town the lane punctuation with MEANING is Lake's lamp ring, which already exists; incidents are secular village life around it. Incidents cluster near homes and thin toward the Gate Field (the unwarm end thins to nothing).

forest._doc: USER RULINGS 2026-08-01: (1) THICKNESS — blockout stage: the forest is the village's CONTAINER, not a rim decoration. Thicken it hard: the wood presses in around and between the outer houses and along the main paths' outer sides, closes every horizon, and swallows the space beyond the infill clusters. Much of the perceived sparseness is missing forest. (2) QUALITY — dressing/bake stage, ON THE RADAR as a hard bar: the low-poly cone trees are placeholders only. The shipped vegetation must read natural/realistic to a modern-2026-game bar IN THE BAKED PLATES (pre-rendered backgrounds can afford film-weight trees at zero runtime cost — that is the architecture's whole advantage). GATE: before mass-producing the forest, a taste PROBE — one fixed camera, 2-3 tree treatments (geometry-node realistic / textured painterly / current stylized) — goes to the user, and the ratified treatment must keep Emberbrook and Dellhollow coherent as one game. | FARMLAND RULING 2026-08-01 (user): cleared land is welcome IF visibly CLAIMED for farming — the objection was never to open ground, it was to unclaimed emptiness between village and treeline. THE RULE: every acre between the village and the wood is either forest or WORKED land — field strips with boundaries (hedges/stone rows/fences), crop rows or autumn stubble, pasture, orchard extensions, haystacks — reading as somebody's livelihood. At blockout: field-parcel massing with boundary lines; at dressing: the crops, stubble, and farm clutter. No ambiguous green voids.

dressing._doc: USER-LOVED 2026-08-01, dressing-tier (district pass, not landmarks): stepping stones at one informal brook crossing; terraced kitchen gardens behind cottages; root-cellar doors in the Home Row rise; hay stooks + threshing floor by the tithe barn; lantern-maker's workbench (wicks, oil jars, glass) near the item shop; geese on the washline green; Mochi sunning ledges (waystone top, mill windowsill); drying racks + upturned skiff at the jetty. EXCLUDED BY RULING: wayside shrines (the Heartlight owns meaning) and fae-flavored anything (the Whisperwood's strangeness is Act 2 property).

coexistence._doc: USER RULING 2026-08-01 (the town-model review — supersedes styling details of earlier rulings where they conflict): 'This is a village that has stood itself up in the middle of a dense forest, and it coexists peacefully with nature rather than stripping away all nature to make space for its houses.' THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) HOUSEHOLD BOUNDARIES lose the suburban trimmed-hedge vocabulary — irregular stone rows, split-rail/paling fragments, bramble clumps, PARTIAL enclosure; claimed, not manicured. (2) VILLAGE TREES: large individual trees scattered AMONG the houses and over the lanes — several species shapes and sizes (broadleaf crowns + slimmer forms alongside the forest conifers), so the wood visibly continues through the village. Blockout: varied canopy massing; QUALITY stays the dressing-stage bar. (3) THE SQUARE IS A CONTAINED ROOM: more buildings + trees closing the ring around Festival Square so it reads as its own space.
